mechanism: Keep one compact identity board visually unchanged while a separate live area verifies the same subject through several functionally different proofs. Vary pose, distance, camera angle and movement silhouette, then reserve one late high-complexity skill proof; the board is a continuous comparison standard, not decoration.

invariants.rule: Keep one compact identity board unchanged and readable throughout.
invariants.ablation_failure: A changing board removes the comparison standard.

invariants.rule: Verify the same subject across at least three different live-view scales or poses.
invariants.purpose: Tests identity beyond one flattering frame.
invariants.ablation_failure: Repeated copies of the same pose do not prove stability.

invariants.rule: Give each live phase a different verification duty, including at least one full movement silhouette.
invariants.ablation_failure: Decorative angle changes cannot validate identity.

invariants.rule: Preserve key identity anchors through camera-angle and motion changes.
invariants.ablation_failure: Losing face, silhouette and costume anchors makes the board irrelevant.

invariants.rule: Reserve one late complex skill proof and hold it beside the unchanged board.
invariants.ablation_failure: Ending on the board alone reads like documentation, not completed live proof.

slots.name: lead_subject
slots.constraint: An original stable subject or pair with a readable role.

slots.name: setting
slots.constraint: A new setting with fixed spatial anchors and no source-specific surface.

slots.name: escalation_variable
slots.constraint: One causal variable that changes through visible stages.

slots.name: performance_rule
slots.constraint: A restrained acting or motion rule that keeps the mechanism legible.

slots.name: camera_grammar
slots.constraint: An information order that proves each state without copying source shot boundaries.

slots.name: payoff
slots.constraint: A clean final physical, informational or social consequence.

slots.name: sound_family
slots.constraint: An original hierarchy of diegetic cues; no unsupported source-audio claim.
